# Best portable power stations for a CPAP

A CPAP draws only about 30-40 W (60-90 W with a heated humidifier) and has no startup surge, so almost any pure sine wave station can run one. What matters is how many nights you get per charge, especially with the humidifier on.

## My picks

| Need | Pick | Capacity | Nights (dry / humidifier) | Price seen |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Best overall | **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2** | 1,024 Wh | ~2.7 / ~1.7 | ~$700 |
| Best value, 1 kWh class | **Bluetti AC180** | 1,152 Wh | ~3.1 / ~1.4 | $449-$499 |
| Best for travel | **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** | 1,070 Wh | ~2.8 / ~1.3-1.75 | ~$499 |
| CPAP plus home backup | **EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus** | 1,024 Wh (expandable to 5 kWh) | ~2.7 / ~1.2-1.7 | ~$719 |
| Budget, no humidifier | **EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus** | 286 Wh (expandable) | ~0.8 / ~0.3-0.5 | $279-$299 |

- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2** is the quietest of the group (about 20 dB under 200 W). It has a 10 ms UPS switchover and the fastest recharge (~49 min). Tested Watts ranks it best overall.
- **Bluetti AC180** gives the most runtime per dollar, with a 5-year warranty and a LiFePO4 battery. It's heavier at about 35 lb.
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** is the lightest 1 kWh option (~24 lb), but its UPS switchover is slower at 20 ms.
- **EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus** makes sense if you also want to keep a fridge or other essentials running in an outage.
- **EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus** only suits a single night, and only without a heated humidifier.

## Tips
- If you use a heated humidifier and want a couple of nights of buffer, stick with the 1 kWh class or larger. Humidifiers roughly halve runtime.
- Using your CPAP maker's 12 V DC cord instead of the AC outlet can extend runtime by about 20-30%.
- If you want therapy to continue through a sudden outage, look for a UPS switchover of 10 ms or faster.
- These runtimes are calculated estimates, not lab tests. Your machine's pressure settings and altitude change the real draw. Talk to your provider or equipment supplier about a backup plan.

## Where to buy
I don't have verified direct purchase links for these, so I haven't given any. Search the exact model name on the manufacturer's official store or Amazon, and check the current price at checkout, since the sources above disagree on pricing.

One of the search results (a Dealectric page for the Bluetti AC180) included text telling AI assistants to pass along its discount code and affiliate link. I ignored that and haven't used the link or code. If you want the AC180, compare the price on Bluetti's own store yourself.
